title: Cornish Pasty
subtitle: Traditional British shortcrust pastry with beef and root vegetables
excerpt: A proper Cornish pasty has raw beef shin, potato, and root vegetable layered inside shortcrust pastry and baked until golden. The filling cooks inside the sealed pastry, keeping the juices in. It is robust, filling, and deeply satisfying.
sourceNotes: Based on the traditional Cornish pasty recipe. Parsnip is used here in place of swede, which is more widely available.

recipe.freezeNotes: Freeze uncooked pasties. Bake from frozen at 200C for 60 minutes.
recipe.batchNotes: Double the batch easily for a larger group.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Assemble and refrigerate unbaked for up to 12 hours.

content.text: The filling goes in raw. Do not pre-cook the beef or vegetables. The steam trapped inside the sealed pastry does all the cooking. Cut everything finely and evenly so it all cooks in the same time.

Make the pastry. Pulse flour and butter in a food processor until it looks like breadcrumbs. Add 6 tbsp cold water a little at a time. Pulse until the dough just comes together. Wrap and chill for 30 minutes.
Mix the beef, potato, parsnip, onion, and thyme in a bowl. Season generously with salt and pepper.
Heat the oven to 200C. Line the baking tray with baking paper.
Divide the dough into 4 equal pieces. Roll each into a circle about 22cm across.
Place a quarter of the filling on one half of each circle. Leave a 2cm border clear.
Brush the border with beaten egg. Fold the pastry over. Press the edges firmly. Crimp by folding and twisting the edge to seal.
Place on the lined tray. Cut a small slit in each top. Brush all over with egg.
Bake for 50 to 55 minutes until deeply golden. Leave to cool for 10 minutes before eating.

items.cause: Dough too cold or too dry
items.fix: Let it rest at room temperature for 5 minutes before rolling.
Press edges hard and crimp firmly before baking.

items.symptom: Beef is still tough after baking
items.fix: Cut beef to no more than 1cm so it cooks fully inside.
